disease_mechanism_summary: TSC is caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in TSC1 or TSC2 with a somatic second hit in lesions (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:8824721). Loss of TSC2 GAP activity leaves RHEB GTP-bound and mTORC1 constitutively active, driving growth, translation, autophagy suppression and disturbed neuronal migration/excitability. The mechanism is validated in humans: rapalogs shrink SEGA and angiomyolipoma (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:24729041; NCT00789828) and reduce refractory seizures (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:30169322). The unresolved part is neurological. Real-world everolimus seizure response is ~31% (46% children vs 14% adults) (EVIDENCE, inconclusive, PMID:38042867), and EEG abnormality at ~42 weeks postmenstrual age already predicts 24-month cognitive and ASD outcome (EVIDENCE, PMID:33178126) — consistent with a substantial prenatally patterned, mTOR-inhibitor-unreachable component. Whether residual seizures reflect insufficient brain target engagement or fixed circuit pathology is the single pivotal uncertainty (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied). Lesion regrowth after rapalog withdrawal shows the action is cytostatic/suppressive (INFERENCE, inconclusive, PMID:24729041).
leverage_points: Depth of brain mTOR target engagement: rapamycin-resistant 4E-BP1 phosphorylation in cortex is a measurable, drug-addressable node that everolimus does not normalize; brain-penetrant catalytic inhibitors normalize it and reduce seizures in Tsc models (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:37399505; PMID:37545094).

Timing rather than molecule: the presymptomatic window is objectively detectable — epileptiform discharges preceded seizures in 54/94 seizure-naive TSC infants under monthly video-EEG (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:33180985), and first-EEG timing/features predict 24-month outcome (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:33778971).

Age-dependent reversibility: the 46% vs 14% child/adult everolimus response gap implies young patients retain signalling-dependent, therefore drug-addressable, disease (INFERENCE, inconclusive, PMID:38042867).

An untested natural experiment already exists: infants dosed with sirolimus/everolimus in the first months of life for cardiac rhabdomyoma while still seizure-naive — a causal-pathway presymptomatic exposure readable retrospectively (INFERENCE, supportive).
Therapeutic-window engineering (pulsed catalytic dosing, or low-dose rapalog plus intermittent catalytic) as the only realistic way to exploit deeper inhibition in children (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).

reviews.why_it_could_work: Human proof that mTOR inhibition is anti-seizure in TSC already exists (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:30169322), and the stated deficiency of rapalogs — partial mTORC1 inhibition plus poor brain permeability — is concrete and measurable as persistent cortical p4E-BP1. Brain-penetrant ATP-competitive inhibitors were built for exactly this gap, normalized brain mTOR signalling and extended survival in neuronal Tsc1-KO mice (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:37399505), and TC1 reduced seizure burden in a Tsc2 hypomorph with spontaneous seizures (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:37545094). The chemical class is mature (vistusertib, sapanisertib, AZD8055 reached Phase 1-2; ChEMBL CHEMBL2842).
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: Mechanism-based collapse of the therapeutic window. Removing the mTORC2 sparing that makes rapalogs chronically tolerable risks immunosuppression, metabolic and growth effects and loss of neuronal mTORC2 in a developing child (INFERENCE/HYPOTHESIS, contradictory). This failure mode is entirely untested — no chronic juvenile tolerability study exists. Compounding it: no de-risked chemical starting point. Published brain-penetrant leads are explicitly tool compounds with in vitro genotoxicity, poor oral exposure in higher species and dose-limiting cynomolgus toxicity (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:37399505); oncology catalytic inhibitors never produced a chronically dosable agent (INFERENCE, contradictory, ChEMBL CHEMBL2842); no TSC trial of a catalytic mTOR inhibitor was identified (EVIDENCE, contradictory, ClinicalTrials.gov 'Tuberous sclerosis complex'). The upstream NO EXISTING AGENT IDENTIFIED label is correct.
reviews.rationale: The proposed head-to-head is a genuine kill experiment: it pre-registers a pharmacodynamic acceptance criterion (cortical p4E-BP1 indistinguishable from wild-type) so a negative efficacy result is interpretable rather than a dosing failure, pairs EEG with free unbound brain concentration, and doses after seizure onset — the clinically relevant hard case. It gates a multi-year discovery programme against a cheap mouse study. Two reservations keep this at INVESTIGATE rather than PURSUE. First, it answers the efficacy premise but not the dominant failure mode; I would require the chronic juvenile tolerability arm and the pulsed/combination arm funded in the same package, since a positive efficacy result with an uncloseable window is still a dead programme. Second, germline biallelic mouse models carry more uniform and severe mTOR activation than the mosaic human two-hit lesion, and no mouse reproduces human tubers with giant cells, so deep inhibition will likely look better in mouse than in patients (INFERENCE, inconclusive). A positive result licenses a window-engineering programme, not a candidate.

reviews.why_it_could_work: The window is proven to exist and be detectable: epileptiform discharges preceded clinical seizures in 54 of 94 seizure-naive TSC infants under monthly video-EEG (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:33180985), and first-EEG timing and features predict epilepsy and 24-month neurodevelopmental outcome, earlier in TSC2 (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:33778971). Early vigabatrin may reduce refractory epilepsy and spasms (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:38865948). Critically, both candidate agents are approved with established paediatric dosing and proven functional CNS engagement in children (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:30169322; PMID:37638552) — this needs trial design and surveillance infrastructure, not new chemistry, the lowest pharmacological risk of the three. And the arm with the strongest causal rationale, presymptomatic mTOR inhibition, has never been tested (EVIDENCE, not_studied, ClinicalTrials.gov 'Tuberous sclerosis complex').
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: Repeating PREVeNT. That randomized double-blind trial of vigabatrin at first epileptiform EEG found no improvement in Bayley-III cognition at 24 months and no reduction in focal seizures (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:37638552), with 36-month follow-up showing cognitive decline in all groups and no prevention of intellectual disability or ASD (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:41061327). The structural failure matters as much as the biological one: 19 of 27 placebo infants crossed to open-label vigabatrin at median 44 days, collapsing the exposure contrast (EVIDENCE, inconclusive, PMID:37638552); EPISTOP could not randomize at 4 of 10 centres and needed bias-corrected re-analysis (EVIDENCE, inconclusive, PMID:39625912). Biologically the plausible killer is that TAND is largely prenatally fixed — EEG at ~42 weeks postmenstrual age already predicts 24-month outcome (EVIDENCE, PMID:33178126). Add vigabatrin's irreversible retinal toxicity, now unoffset by demonstrated cognitive benefit (INFERENCE, contradictory, PMID:31912454).
reviews.rationale: This is the only approach where the experiment is both cheap and decision-complete, and where the proposer learned from the field's failure rather than restating its hopes. Step 1 — retrospectively assembling seizure-naive TSC infants incidentally exposed to sirolimus/everolimus for cardiac rhabdomyoma, matched on genotype, tuber burden and first-EEG phenotype, scored blind — exploits an existing human natural experiment, requires no new infant dosing, and tests the causal-pathway arm before anyone spends a cohort on it. Confounding by rhabdomyoma severity is real but manageable by matching, an acceptable price for a signal that gates a trial (INFERENCE, inconclusive). Step 2's design fix is the substantive contribution: permitting open-label vigabatrin rescue in both arms so the randomized contrast is mTOR inhibition alone structurally removes the crossover that destroyed PREVeNT (INFERENCE, PMID:37638552). I explicitly endorse powering on seizure/EEG endpoints with cognition secondary — given PREVeNT and the predictive first EEG, powering on cognition is the most likely way to waste the only realistic infant prevention cohort. PURSUE is earned by human causal evidence, approved agents, validated endpoints and a cheap gating step. The honest caveat is that the ceiling may be epilepsy trajectory only; that is still worth having, and Step 1 will say so before anyone is dosed.

reviews.why_it_could_work: The targets are extracellular, the one genuine advantage of a biologic here. Astrocyte-localized IL-1b and CXCL10 are elevated in neocortex and hippocampus of Tsc1-GFAP CKO mice, a defined neutralizable ligand (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:26003087). Brain VEGF is elevated with abnormal vessel anatomy and two-photon-confirmed BBB leak (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:38049961). VEGFR2 is luminal on endothelium, so an approved ligand trap engages target without crossing the BBB (INFERENCE, supportive), and anakinra has human precedent in refractory epilepsy/FIRES establishing tolerability (EVIDENCE, supportive for tolerability only, PMID:33681649).
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: The two arms' advantages do not combine, and this is decisive. The IL-1 arm has the seizure-proximal astrocyte-localized story but no parenchymal delivery path: standard subcutaneous anakinra reaches only a small single-digit percent of plasma concentration in CSF, and no BBB-shuttle-engineered IL-1Ra or anti-IL-1b exists — TfR1 shuttle platforms are clinical-stage for enzymes but never applied to cytokine blockade, making this de novo engineering, not repurposing (INFERENCE, contradictory). The VEGF arm has the delivery but the weaker story, plus chronic systemic anti-angiogenesis in growing children with existing angiomyolipoma bleeding risk is a poor risk fit (INFERENCE, contradictory). Underneath both sits the target-validity problem: the inflammatory markers were themselves reversed by mTORC1 inhibition, the signature of a downstream readout rather than an independent driver (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:26003087). A TSC + anakinra ClinicalTrials.gov search returned 0 studies (EVIDENCE, contradictory). The upstream NO PLAUSIBLE DELIVERY PATH conclusion is correct.
reviews.rationale: I accept the proposed ICV experiment as scientifically well-posed while rejecting the programme, and these are not in tension. The design is right where it matters: it bypasses the BBB entirely by chronic intracerebroventricular minipump to maximize the chance of a positive signal, tests on top of submaximal rapamycin rather than as monotherapy, and requires documented CSF exposure and cortical IL-1R engagement so a null is interpretable. That makes it a true ceiling test — if saturating CNS IL-1Ra adds nothing to rapamycin, no shuttle engineering can rescue the arm and the node is killed permanently. But a positive ICV result in mouse does not create a human delivery path and would not de-risk the human route (INFERENCE, contradictory); it would only license an expensive multi-year BBB-shuttle or intrathecal feasibility programme. Given the most likely outcome is null on prior evidence (PMID:26003087), a protein programme should not be funded now. The experiment is worth running only as a cheap rider on the small-molecule add-on study, which is exactly how it was proposed. REJECT applies to the biologic programme, not to the question.

reviews.why_it_could_work: The model reproduces the phenotype and the intervention is executable today with off-the-shelf compounds: Tsc1-GFAP CKO mice show elevated brain VEGF, abnormal vessel anatomy and two-photon-confirmed BBB leak, with apatinib and RepSox already applied as interventions (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:38049961), and astrocytic IL-1b/CXCL10 elevation with anti-inflammatory treatment tested against epilepsy in the same model (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:26003087). If any part of the axis were mTOR-independent it would offer seizure benefit without full mTOR suppression — valuable precisely where the catalytic approach fails on tolerability (INFERENCE, supportive).
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: Epiphenomenon. The markers are reversed by mTORC1 inhibition alone (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:26003087), so the single most likely result is zero incremental benefit. A second, independent failure is agent-level and would bite even on a positive result: apatinib is a P-gp substrate with limited CNS exposure and is China-only, RepSox is a non-clinical tool compound, so no translatable molecule emerges (INFERENCE, contradictory, PMID:38049961); chronic VEGFR inhibition in children causes hypertension, impaired wound healing and growth-plate effects (INFERENCE, contradictory); no agent of this class appears in the TSC clinical pipeline (EVIDENCE, contradictory, ClinicalTrials.gov 'Tuberous sclerosis complex'). There is also a cell-type mismatch: the readily drugged compartment (endothelium) is not clearly the seizure-driving compartment (astrocyte/neuron).
reviews.rationale: The factorial add-on design is the correct and economical way to ask this question and is better specified than the hypothesis deserves. Using a submaximal rapamycin reference arm titrated to ~50% seizure-burden reduction is the key move — rapamycin is near-curative in this model and would otherwise compress the ceiling so no add-on effect could be detected. Including a near-maximal rapamycin ceiling arm, dosing from P21 after symptom onset, and making brain-tissue drug concentration plus target engagement (cortical phospho-VEGFR2; cortical mature IL-1b) a mandatory gate means a null is interpretable rather than a dosing artifact. At a few hundred thousand dollars and 6-9 months it is a legitimate go/no-go. It ranks below the other two not because the experiment is poor but because even the supportive branch does not hand you a molecule: it buys the right to start de novo CNS-penetrant chemistry on the IL-1 node, from a single-model evidence base. LOW PRIORITY means run it as a rider if a Tsc1-GFAP CKO EEG colony is already running — with the protein-arm ICV cohort attached — not as a standalone programme. Apatinib or any chronic systemic anti-angiogenic should not advance into a paediatric lifelong indication regardless of outcome.

comparative_judgment:
These three approaches fail in different places, and the ranking follows where the failure sits rather than how good the mechanism sounds.

Presymptomatic intervention is the only approach whose binding constraint is trial design rather than pharmacology or delivery. The agents are approved with paediatric dosing and proven CNS engagement, the window is objectively detectable by EEG (PMID:33180985), the endpoints are validated and already collected (PMID:33778971; PMID:33178126), and decisively the gating step is a retrospective cohort requiring no new infant dosing. The causal-pathway arm, presymptomatic mTOR inhibition, has never been tested while the GABAergic arm has already been falsified for cognition (PMID:37638552; PMID:41061327). That combination of untested causal rationale plus near-zero-cost first step earns PURSUE.

Catalytic mTOR inhibition has the strongest mechanistic logic and real in vivo seizure data (PMID:37545094), but its dominant failure mode — chronic TORC1/2 tolerability in children — is completely untested, and there is no de-risked chemical starting point (PMID:37399505). It sits at INVESTIGATE rather than PURSUE precisely because a compelling mechanism must not outrank an untested window and absent chemistry. The proposed experiment tests efficacy, not the failure mode; fund it only bundled with the chronic juvenile tolerability and pulsed/combination arms.

On the two modalities for the downstream axis, the same hypothesis splits cleanly. The small-molecule version is testable now with off-the-shelf compounds in a well-designed factorial add-on and gets LOW PRIORITY; the protein version is REJECTed because the arm with the better biology (IL-1, astrocyte-localized) has no parenchymal delivery path and the arm with the delivery (luminal VEGF) has the weaker story and an unacceptable paediatric chronic-dosing profile. The advantages sit in different arms and do not combine. Both share one upstream liability: the markers are reversed by mTORC1 inhibition (PMID:26003087), the signature of an epiphenomenon. The cheap route is to run the ICV protein cohort as a rider on the small-molecule add-on study and settle both at once.

What would change my mind. On prevention: a null retrospective signal, or benefit disappearing after adjustment for TSC2 status and tuber burden, would stop another presymptomatic rapalog trial outright — chronic everolimus immunosuppression in asymptomatic infants cannot be justified on hope. On catalytic inhibition: demonstrated normalization of cortical p4E-BP1 producing seizure freedom in everolimus-refractory animals together with a tolerable pulsed regimen in juvenile mice would move it to PURSUE; conversely, benefit only at exposures abolishing systemic pAKT-S473 would kill it. On the downstream axis: incremental seizure reduction surviving a near-maximal rapamycin ceiling arm with documented brain target engagement would promote the small-molecule arm to INVESTIGATE, and would be the only result justifying revisiting the protein arm's delivery engineering.
what_is_known: Human randomized proof of mechanism exists: everolimus shrinks SEGA and angiomyolipoma (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:24729041; NCT00789828) and reduces treatment-refractory seizures (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:30169322).
Efficacy on the neurological axis is partial and age-dependent: ~31% real-world seizure response, 46% in children vs 14% in adults (EVIDENCE, inconclusive, PMID:38042867).

A clearly failed approach: PREVeNT, randomized double-blind placebo-controlled vigabatrin at first epileptiform EEG, showed no Bayley-III cognitive benefit at 24 months and no reduction in focal seizures (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:37638552), with no prevention of intellectual disability or ASD at 36 months (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:41061327).

Both prevention trials are compromised as prevention tests: PREVeNT lost exposure contrast when 19/27 placebo infants crossed to open-label vigabatrin at median 44 days (EVIDENCE, inconclusive, PMID:37638552); EPISTOP could not randomize at 4 of 10 centres (EVIDENCE, inconclusive, PMID:39625912).

The presymptomatic window is real and detectable: epileptiform discharges preceded seizures in 54/94 seizure-naive infants (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:33180985); first-EEG timing predicts 24-month outcome (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:33778971).
Much of the relevant biology precedes any postnatal drug: EEG at ~42 weeks postmenstrual age already predicts 24-month ASD risk and developmental quotient (EVIDENCE, PMID:33178126).

Brain-penetrant catalytic mTOR inhibitors exist but only as tool compounds: in vitro genotoxicity, poor oral exposure in higher species, dose-limiting cynomolgus toxicity (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:37399505); TC1 nonetheless reduced seizures in a Tsc2 hypomorph (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:37545094).
The ATP-competitive class is chemically mature but never produced a chronically dosable agent (vistusertib, sapanisertib, AZD8055; ChEMBL CHEMBL2842) (INFERENCE, contradictory).

No TSC trial of a catalytic mTOR inhibitor, of presymptomatic mTOR inhibition, or of IL-1/VEGF blockade for epilepsy was identified (EVIDENCE, ClinicalTrials.gov 'Tuberous sclerosis complex'; TSC+anakinra returned 0 studies).
Neuroinflammatory markers in Tsc1-GFAP CKO are reversed by mTORC1 inhibition — the signature of a downstream readout (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:26003087).
Lesions regrow after rapalog withdrawal: the action is suppressive, implying lifelong therapy (INFERENCE, inconclusive, PMID:24729041).
Vigabatrin carries irreversible retinal toxicity, now unoffset by demonstrated cognitive benefit (INFERENCE, contradictory, PMID:31912454).
critical_gaps: Whether residual seizures on maximal rapalog reflect insufficient brain target engagement (persistent cortical p4E-BP1 phosphorylation) or fixed circuit pathology. The catalytic programme cannot be costed until this is answered.
Whether chronic TORC1/2 inhibition at brain-effective exposure is tolerable in juveniles. This is the dominant failure mode of the catalytic approach and no model or study currently addresses it.
Whether presymptomatic mTOR inhibition changes epilepsy trajectory in seizure-naive infants — the one arm with a causal rationale that has never been tested.
How much TAND is prenatally fixed versus driven by postnatal epileptiform activity. PREVeNT gives the first serious negative answer for a GABAergic drug; the causal-pathway equivalent is unknown.
Whether any part of the neurovascular/neuroinflammatory axis is mTOR-independent. All retrieved evidence is consistent with pure downstream readout.
No model reproduces human cortical tubers with giant cells or perituberal laminar disorganization; target engagement in human tuber tissue is modelled only by proxy (INFERENCE, inconclusive).
No de-risked chemical starting point for a CNS-optimized, non-genotoxic, P-gp-sparing catalytic mTOR inhibitor (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:37399505).

next_actions.action: Assemble, from TSC centres and registries, every infant who received sirolimus or everolimus in the first 6 months of life for cardiac rhabdomyoma or another non-epilepsy indication while still seizure-naive, matched to unexposed seizure-naive TSC infants on genotype (TSC2 vs TSC1), MRI tuber burden and first-EEG phenotype; score outcomes blind to exposure.
next_actions.question_answered: Does starting an mTOR inhibitor before clinical seizure onset change the epilepsy trajectory in TSC infants?
next_actions.activity_required: Retrospective multi-centre cohort assembly and blinded chart/EEG review; 6-12 months; no new dosing.
next_actions.supports_if: Materially later first seizure or lower drug-resistant epilepsy rate (e.g. HR <=0.6) surviving adjustment for genotype and tuber burden, ideally with a dose/timing gradient. Fund the Step 2 randomized trial.
next_actions.kills_if: No shift in seizure timing or epilepsy severity despite months of presymptomatic exposure, or benefit vanishing on adjustment for TSC2 status and tuber burden. Do not run another presymptomatic rapalog trial.

next_actions.action: Run the pharmacodynamically anchored head-to-head seizure study in the Tsc2 hypomorph (cross-checked in Tsc1-GFAP CKO), treating after seizure onset: maximal tolerated everolimus vs a brain-penetrant catalytic tool compound titrated to normalize cortical p4E-BP1 vs everolimus plus pulsed catalytic vs vehicle, with continuous video-EEG, regional pS6/p4E-BP1/pAKT-S473 and unbound brain and plasma concentrations. Pre-register the PD acceptance criterion.
next_actions.question_answered: Are residual seizures target-engagement-limited or circuit-fixed?
next_actions.activity_required: Pilot PK/PD dose-finding cohort then 3-4 week blinded EEG study with matched terminal PD cohorts; powered for a 50% between-arm difference.
next_actions.supports_if: The catalytic arm normalizes cortical p4E-BP1 where everolimus does not and delivers substantially greater seizure reduction (seizure freedom or >75% vs ~30-40%) in everolimus-refractory animals. Proceed to the window question, not to chemistry.
next_actions.kills_if: Confirmed p4E-BP1 normalization yields no additional seizure benefit, or benefit only at exposures that abolish systemic pAKT-S473 and cause weight loss/overt toxicity. Do not fund CNS-optimized catalytic chemistry for epilepsy.

next_actions.action: In the same colony, run a chronic juvenile tolerability study of the pulsed/low-dose-rapalog-plus-intermittent-catalytic regimen: growth, immune competence, metabolic parameters and neurodevelopmental behaviour over a developmentally relevant dosing period.
next_actions.question_answered: Can deep mTOR kinase inhibition be dosed chronically in a developing animal at brain-effective exposure?
next_actions.activity_required: Juvenile chronic dosing cohort with growth, immunophenotyping, metabolic panel and behavioural battery; run in parallel with, not after, the efficacy study.
next_actions.supports_if: An intermittent or combination regimen preserves brain p4E-BP1 suppression while sparing systemic pAKT-S473, with normal growth and immune competence. The programme becomes a tractable window-engineering problem.
next_actions.kills_if: No regimen separates brain efficacy from systemic mTORC2 loss, growth failure or immunosuppression. The differentiating pharmacology can never be dosed in children; stop.

next_actions.action: Run the factorial add-on study in Tsc1-GFAP CKO mice against a submaximal rapamycin reference arm (titrated to ~50% seizure-burden reduction) with a near-maximal rapamycin ceiling arm, testing apatinib and IL-1 axis blockade, with brain drug concentration and target engagement as a mandatory gate; attach the chronic ICV IL-1Ra cohort as a rider.
next_actions.question_answered: Is any part of the neurovascular/neuroinflammatory axis an mTOR-independent causal seizure driver?
next_actions.activity_required: Six-arm randomized blinded mouse EEG study, n~12-15/arm, both sexes, dosed from P21; 6-9 months; plus ICV minipump cohort with CSF exposure and cortical IL-1R engagement.
next_actions.supports_if: Pre-specified incremental seizure-burden reduction (e.g. >=40%) over submaximal rapamycin with documented brain target engagement, ideally persisting against the near-maximal ceiling arm.
next_actions.kills_if: No incremental benefit despite confirmed brain target engagement and confirmed suppression of the axis biomarker — including saturating ICV IL-1Ra. Closes both the small-molecule and protein arms permanently.

next_actions.action: Design, contingent on action 1, a randomized trial of everolimus added at first epileptiform EEG, powered on EEG/seizure endpoints with cognition secondary, pre-specifying open-label vigabatrin rescue permitted in BOTH arms so the randomized contrast is mTOR inhibition alone.
next_actions.question_answered: Does presymptomatic mTOR inhibition prevent drug-resistant epilepsy, and can a prevention trial survive rescue crossover?
next_actions.activity_required: Prospective multi-centre EEG-triggered randomized trial with serial video-EEG surveillance infrastructure.
next_actions.supports_if: Lower epileptiform EEG burden and higher proportion seizure-free at 24 months in the everolimus arm.
next_actions.kills_if: No seizure/EEG separation despite documented exposure, confirming the trajectory is set before postnatal intervention can act.

do_not_fund_yet: De novo CNS-optimized ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor chemistry (lead optimization, tox packages). There is no de-risked starting point and the premise that deeper engagement converts non-responders is untested; the mouse PD/EEG study settles this for the price of one study (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:37399505).

Any clinical trial of a catalytic mTOR inhibitor in TSC children before a chronic juvenile tolerability study exists. The dominant failure mode is the therapeutic window and it is currently unmeasured.

A BBB-shuttle-engineered IL-1Ra or anti-IL-1b programme. This is de novo engineering, not repurposing, and should not be entered without a positive saturating-ICV result in hand (INFERENCE, contradictory).

Any chronic systemic anti-angiogenic (apatinib or other VEGFR TKI, bevacizumab) in a paediatric lifelong TSC indication, regardless of mouse outcome — hypertension, growth-plate and wound-healing toxicity on top of existing angiomyolipoma bleeding risk (INFERENCE, contradictory).
Another presymptomatic vigabatrin trial powered on cognitive endpoints. PREVeNT and its 36-month follow-up have answered this (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:37638552; PMID:41061327).
Any infant prevention trial powered primarily on cognition. Given that the first EEG already predicts 24-month outcome (PMID:33178126), this is the most likely way to waste the one realistic cohort.

A biologic monotherapy arm in the downstream axis. The add-on-to-rapamycin design is the only one that distinguishes an independent driver from a reversible readout (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:26003087).
conclusion_note: The mechanism is established and human-validated, so the disease can be responsibly planned — but the decision has moved from target to timing and therapeutic window. Presymptomatic mTOR inhibition is the only PURSUE, gated on a cheap retrospective natural experiment. Catalytic mTOR inhibition is mechanistically attractive but has no existing agent and an untested paediatric window. The downstream neurovascular/neuroinflammatory axis is most likely an epiphenomenon; its protein modality additionally has no plausible delivery path.
